children: Swedish defence and aerospace group Saab
reported on Friday a bigger-than-expected rise in third-quarter profit on the back of soaring sales as it continued to ride a wave of global rearmament.
Operating profit at the maker of the Gripen fighter jet rose to 1.95 billion crowns ($197 million) from 1.37 billion a year earlier, against a 1.91 billion mean forecast in an LSEG poll of analysts.

"The long-term market outlook remains favourable," CEO Micael Johansson said in a statement. "With a strong portfolio, a record high order backlog, expanding production capacity and continued investment in future capabilities, we are well positioned to achieve our financial targets," he said.
Saab, which also makes military equipment ranging from missiles and advanced electronics to submarines, said in a statement like-for-like sales rose 30.6% year-on-year.
